Two small molecules from `files/`: toluene and a dimethoxy-benzodithiophene. Each is substituted with
fragments from the built-in library and relaxed with the default RDKit force field.

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `files/tol.xyz` — toluene, C7H8 (15 atoms); H 10 sits on the para carbon C 4
* `files/geom.xyz` — dimethoxy-benzodithiophene, C12H10O2S2 (26 atoms); thiophene α-H 17 on C 6 and H 19 on C 9

**1. One fragment on one site.** Replace the para H of toluene (atom 10) by a phenyl bonded to C 4.

```bash
frog-substitute --mol files/tol.xyz --mol-pairs 10 4 --db-frag phenyl --out-dir subs
```

```text
ℹ  Processing base molecule: tol.xyz
ℹ  Substituting with fragment 'phenyl'...
✔      RDKit force-field relaxation complete. Core RMSD: 0.0000 A.
✔  Saved geometry: subs/tol_phenyl.xyz
                      Fragment Substitution Summary
╭──────────┬──────────┬─────────┬───────────────┬───────┬────────────────╮
│ Molecule │ Fragment │ Status  │ Core RMSD (Å) │ Atoms │ Output File    │
├──────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┼───────┼────────────────┤
│ tol.xyz  │ phenyl   │ SUCCESS │        0.0000 │    25 │ tol_phenyl.xyz │
╰──────────┴──────────┴─────────┴───────────────┴───────┴────────────────╯
```

`subs/tol_phenyl.xyz` (first 4 lines):

```text
25
Properties=species:S:1:pos:R:3:move_mask:L:1 pbc="F F F"
C       -0.01214700       1.19710000       0.00040000  F
C       -0.70334700       0.00000000       0.00010000  F
…
```

* 25 atoms: the 15 atoms of toluene, minus H 10, plus the 11 atoms of C6H5. The phenyl file in the library
  has one more atom: the H at Delete index 0, which is removed.
* Core RMSD 0.0000 Å: none of the 14 toluene atoms that are kept has moved. The removed H was the last
  hydrogen of the ring, so atoms 0–9 keep their indices, and the phenyl atoms are appended at the end.
* The XYZ is written in extended format. The extra `move_mask` column holds the frozen-atom constraint of the
  relaxation: `F` for the scaffold, `T` for the fragment atoms.

**2. A scope preset.** All halogens on the same site, plus one multi-structure file for viewing.

```bash
frog-substitute --mol files/tol.xyz --mol-pairs 10 4 --scope halogens --out-dir subs --combined-xyz subs/tol_halogens.xyz -q
```

```text
                      Fragment Substitution Summary
╭──────────┬──────────┬─────────┬───────────────┬───────┬────────────────╮
│ Molecule │ Fragment │ Status  │ Core RMSD (Å) │ Atoms │ Output File    │
├──────────┼──────────┼─────────┼───────────────┼───────┼────────────────┤
│ tol.xyz  │ fluoro   │ SUCCESS │        0.0000 │    15 │ tol_fluoro.xyz │
│ tol.xyz  │ chloro   │ SUCCESS │        0.0000 │    15 │ tol_chloro.xyz │
│ tol.xyz  │ bromo    │ SUCCESS │        0.0000 │    15 │ tol_bromo.xyz  │
│ tol.xyz  │ iodo     │ SUCCESS │        0.0000 │    15 │ tol_iodo.xyz   │
╰──────────┴──────────┴─────────┴───────────────┴───────┴────────────────╯
```

* `--scope halogens` was resolved to the four presets fluoro, chloro, bromo and iodo. Each product has 15
  atoms, because one H is exchanged for one halogen.
* With `-q` only the table is printed. The four files `subs/tol_<fragment>.xyz` and the 4-frame
  `subs/tol_halogens.xyz` are written anyway.

**3. Two sites at once, with atom tracking.** Both thiophene α-H atoms are replaced by 2-thienyl.
`--track 7 10` labels the two ring S atoms in the output.

```bash
frog-substitute --mol files/geom.xyz --mol-pairs 17 6 19 9 --db-frag 2-thienyl --track 7 10
```

```text

│ Molecule │ Fragment  │ Status  │ Core RMSD (Å) │ Atoms │ Output File        │
├──────────┼───────────┼─────────┼───────────────┼───────┼────────────────────┤
│ geom.xyz │ 2-thienyl │ SUCCESS │        0.0000 │    40 │ geom_2-thienyl.xyz │
╰──────────┴───────────┴─────────┴───────────────┴───────┴────────────────────╯
```

`files/geom_2-thienyl.xyz` (first 13 lines):

```text
40
Properties=species:S:1:pos:R:3:move_mask:L:1:original_id:I:1 http://www.ichemlabs.com=T pbc="F F F"
C        0.29534000      -1.36567000       0.49855000  F       -1
C       -1.06086000      -0.95767000       0.49915000  F       -1
C       -1.30196000       0.43573000       0.50025000  F       -1
C        1.06154000       0.95943000       0.50045000  F       -1
C        1.30274000      -0.43407000       0.49925000  F       -1
C       -2.25976000      -1.78357000       0.49915000  F       -1
C       -3.46246000      -1.19317000       0.50015000  F       -1
S       -3.07496000       0.54633000       0.50125000  F        7
C        2.26054000       1.78523000       0.50105000  F       -1
C        3.46324000       1.19473000       0.50105000  F       -1
S        3.07564000      -0.54477000       0.49935000  F       10
…
```

* The sites are processed in turn: there is one *RDKit force-field relaxation* line per site. The product has
  40 atoms: 26, minus 2 H, plus 2 × 8 (C4H3S). Without `--out-dir`, the file goes next to the input.
* Column 6 is `original_id`. It holds 7 and 10 for the two tracked S atoms, and −1 for every other
  atom (the fragment atoms included).
* The comment line of the input (`http://www.ichemlabs.com`) is carried over as an extended-XYZ key.

**Optional: draw the result.** frog-substitute writes no picture. The short ASE/matplotlib script
below draws the input and output of step 3 side by side.

```bash
python - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg'); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from ase.io import read
from ase.neighborlist import natural_cutoffs, NeighborList
from ase.data import covalent_radii
from ase.data.colors import jmol_colors
b = read('files/geom.xyz'); a = read('files/geom_2-thienyl.xyz')
nb = len(b) - 2   # base atoms kept (two H replaced); the fragment atoms follow
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.8))
for ax, m, title, new0 in [(axs[0], b, 'files/geom.xyz (input)', None),
                           (axs[1], a, 'files/geom_2-thienyl.xyz (output)', nb)]:
    nl = NeighborList(natural_cutoffs(m, mult=0.9), self_interaction=False, bothways=False); nl.update(m)
    p = m.positions
    for i in range(len(m)):
        for j in nl.get_neighbors(i)[0]:
            ax.plot(p[[i, j], 0], p[[i, j], 1], color='0.35', lw=2, zorder=1)
    for i in np.argsort(p[:, 2]):
        z = m.numbers[i]; new = new0 is not None and i >= new0
        ax.scatter(p[i, 0], p[i, 1], s=315 * covalent_radii[z]**2, color=jmol_colors[z],
                   edgecolor='tab:blue' if new else 'k', linewidth=2.2 if new else 0.8, zorder=2)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10); ax.set_aspect('equal'); ax.axis('off')
xl = [ax.get_xlim() for ax in axs]; yl = [ax.get_ylim() for ax in axs]
for ax in axs:
    ax.set_xlim(min(x[0] for x in xl), max(x[1] for x in xl)); ax.set_ylim(min(y[0] for y in yl), max(y[1] for y in yl))
fig.savefig('files/geom_2-thienyl.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
EOF
```

The output geometries are force-field guesses with a frozen scaffold. Reoptimise them with your QM method
before you use them.
